findings.current: Sometimes a dream is so wonderful, so hard to leave behind, that you don’t want to wake up. Even after you do, you keep your eyes closed a while longer, going over everything that happened in it.
findings.defect: The source opens with a standalone observation, “Sometimes that happens,” before explaining the kind of moment. The assembled copy drops that beat, which the accepted baseline preserved.
findings.rationale: The Korean has a separate opening sentence at line 5, followed by the elaboration at line 7.
findings.replacement: Sometimes, that happens. Sometimes a dream is so wonderful, so hard to leave behind, that you don’t want to wake up. Even after you do, you keep your eyes closed a while longer, going over everything that happened in it.

findings.current: He did. Though it was less a proposal than a threat from someone who had my life in his hands.
findings.defect: “Had my life in his hands” conveys control but loses the source’s image of gripping and wielding her lifeline, which makes the threat more active and menacing.
findings.rationale: The Korean describes a threat like holding her lifeline in his fist and shaking it; the accepted baseline’s “toy with my life” retained more of that menace.
findings.replacement: He did. Though it was less a proposal than a threat to toy with my life, which he held in his grasp.

summary: The chapter is mostly faithful, but the assembled copy drops a deliberate one-to-nine/tenth-fact joke and omits a source beat at the opening. One dialogue line also weakens the threat’s specific force.
